question: Does market-adjusting daily return and future monthly realized volatility improve joint or separate forecasts and APO profitability?
architecture: Joint three-task LiMT versus three independent single-task LiMT encoders/experts. Seven fits per seed: two joint, two return, two volatility and one shared volume specialist. 21 fits total; the volume task is identical across label regimes.
return: CRSP total daily return at t+2; adjusted return subtracts the same session's broad US market total return. Signal t, execution t+1 close, earned return t+2.
market: Verified frozen local factors-daily/ff5_daily.csv, Mkt-RF + RF, decimal total returns. This benchmark is not Mkt-RF alone.

volatility.horizon: Full next calendar month after the signal month, using that month's daily total returns.
volatility.statistic: Sample standard deviation, ddof=1, daily-return units, no annualization. Adjusted volatility = std(stock daily returns in month) minus std(market daily returns in same month), not std(stock minus market).
volatility.coverage: At least 15 observations and at least 80% of that month's market trading days. Missing targets remain masked; future outcomes never change inference membership.

volume: Unchanged CRSP raw-share volume-shock label at t+2.
normalization: One mean and sample standard deviation per task, fitted on eligible RAW-regime training labels only, then held fixed and shared across raw and adjusted regimes. No daily cross-sectional target normalization: common market subtraction would cancel exactly under it. Feature normalization remains the frozen base training-only transform.
splits: Base train2008-2014/validation2015-2016/test2017-2025. All variants use the SAME days, purging on the later of t+2 and full next-month label end. Thus December signal months are removed at each split boundary; last test signal is in November2025. No test-based tuning.

training.selection: Joint: validation return IC. Specialists: own-task validation IC, with volatility IC averaged within signal month then across target months. Adam FP32/TF32, full daily cross-sections; deterministic seed+epoch date shuffle. Common initialization from the full author core; training RNG reset seed+100000.

portfolio: Same US APO r=.1, USD1bn nominal per side, 2% target/trade caps, equal-dollar executable legs and original CRSP total-return P&L. Feed physical volume-shock predictions into exp(shock + known five-day log volume); risk weighting uses negative predicted monthly volatility (or monthly excess volatility) directly. No future market term is added to predictions. Negative predicted excess volatility is allowed. Costs: gross, buy5 only, and 10bp all trades including final liquidation. Equal-weight deciles are diagnostics.
inference: Primary four paired full-period APO annual-mean contrasts at 10bp all trades: adjusted-minus-raw for joint and separate; separate-minus-joint within each regime. Holm across four tests, HAC20 with correction/t intervals. Gross and buy5 counterparts form a separate eight-test sensitivity family. IC and error diagnostics use daily units for return/volume and target-month units for volatility; bootstrap/HAC sensitivities report dependence. No daily duplicated monthly volatility labels counted as independent months.
insolvency: If fixed-nominal budgets exhaust NAV, retain the solvent prefix and failure date/equity, mark whole-period CAGR/Sharpe and paired full-period inference unavailable; never silently omit a failed system or fabricate post-failure returns.
limits: Retrospective follow-up on an already inspected panel. Changing daily range volatility to monthly realized volatility and global target scaling is controlled by a matched raw-monthly experiment; comparisons with earlier range/CS-normalized results do not isolate market adjustment. Joint selects on return IC while specialists select their own targets. Simple market subtraction is not beta residualization. Neither excess-return labels nor equal dollars guarantee beta neutrality. Ideal execution, assumed shorts, no borrow/financing/impact/slippage beyond stated fees.
